name: Japanese Covered Bridge
kicker: Covered wooden bridge at the west end
summary: The short covered bridge at the west end of the old town, where Nguyễn Thị Minh Khai meets Trần Phú. A small temple sits on the span. Give it about 20 minutes. The build date is unsettled across the official pages, and the ticket for the interior is check on arrival.
heroCaption: The covered bridge from the street, roof on, water in front

notice.title: Confirm the ticket before you pay
notice.body: From 10 August 2026 the city fee is 20,000 VND per person per building. The heritage centre’s January and March 2026 notices still describe 80,000 and 120,000 VND combination tickets, with this bridge as one of the two landmark choices. Ask which one is on sale. The interior hours are also check on arrival.

body: See the roof from the street, then the short wooden passage if the ticket in force includes the interior. Dogs stand at one end and monkeys at the other, with yin-yang tiles overhead. The monument page gives the length as about 18 metres. About 20 minutes is the visit. It is a bridge, and a museum hour is the wrong slot.

The pages do not settle on one build date. The centre’s Vietnamese monument page says Japanese merchants built it in the early 17th century, the temple was added in 1653, and Lord Nguyễn Phúc Chu named it Lai Viễn Kiều in 1719. The French page on the same site says 1593 and, later, the early 17th century. UNESCO’s English list text calls it an 18th-century bridge with a pagoda. Leave all three on the table.

Come in the morning, before the groups, or at the edge of the pedestrian hours. The monument page does not print a door time. In a flood week the river streets can be under water. The bridge page itself does not give a flood line.

figures.caption: The temple altar inside the bridge
figures.alt: Carved wooden altar inside the Japanese Covered Bridge in Hoi An, with an incense burner and offerings

gettingThere: The bridge is at the join of Nguyễn Thị Minh Khai and Trần Phú, at the west end of the ancient town. Walk if you slept in the lanes just off that core. A ride from An Bang has no published minute count. Those minutes are check on arrival.

legs.heading: From the old town
legs.body: Walk to the west end, where Nguyễn Thị Minh Khai meets Trần Phú. The minutes depend on your lane.

legs.heading: From An Bang
legs.body: A ride or a bicycle. No published minute count from the beach to the bridge. Check the minutes on arrival.

closed: No weekly closing day is printed on the monument page.
admissionNote: No separate bridge price is printed on the monument page. From 10 August 2026, Resolution 98/2026 sets 20,000 VND per person per building, the same for a Vietnamese and a foreign visitor. The heritage centre’s 26 January 2026 and 16 March 2026 notices still describe an 80,000 VND ticket (streetscape, Chùa Cầu or Miếu Quan Công, and two other works) and a 120,000 VND ticket (streetscape, one of those landmarks, a museum, and three other works). The March notice says one purchase can be used through the stay, up to three days. A May 2026 article says the town is an open neighbourhood, many people walk in without a ticket, and counts 80,000 VND for four works and 120,000 VND for six. Which desk is in force is check on arrival. The January notice, quoting Resolution 02, lists free entry for Vietnamese disabled people with the certificate, Vietnamese people covered by the 2003 cultural-access decision, children under 16 and pupils, Vietnamese citizens 60 and over, and diplomatic guests. Whether Resolution 98 kept those cases was not on the city portal summary.
